title: Scanner Photo Authentication
subject: Evidence
stem: Peter, a bookkeeper, brought an action against Lydia, an office-equipment dealer, for injuries he sustained when the feeder cover on a desktop check scanner that he had purchased from Lydia shattered while he was using it. At trial, Peter offered a cellphone photograph that he testified he had taken before the incident and that he said fairly and accurately showed the scanner. Lydia called Silas, the technician who had installed the scanner. Silas produced a photograph from a manufacturer's catalog and testified that it fairly and accurately represented the scanner that Peter had purchased from Lydia and that Silas had installed. The scanner in Silas's photograph was plainly different from the scanner in Peter's photograph. Each party objected to the other's photograph.
call: How should the court rule on the objections?

choices.A: Admit only the photograph offered by Peter.
choices.C: Admit both photographs and allow the jury to decide whether either accurately represents the scanner at issue.
choices.D: Admit only the photograph offered by Lydia.

rightExplanation: Both photographs should be admitted. A photograph is authenticated by evidence sufficient to support a finding that it fairly and accurately depicts what it purports to show. Peter supplied that foundation for his cellphone photograph by testifying that he took it before the incident and that it showed the scanner. Silas supplied that foundation for the catalog photograph by testifying that it fairly and accurately represented the scanner Peter bought and Silas installed. The photographs conflict, but that conflict affects weight and credibility. The jury decides which witness, if either, to believe.

wrongExplanations.A: Peter's personal photograph is attractive because he took it before the incident and identified it himself. The breaker is that Silas also gave a sufficient foundation for Lydia's photograph.
wrongExplanations.B: The inconsistent images make exclusion of both seem evenhanded. The breaker is that authentication requires a sufficient foundation, not undisputed proof that the image is accurate.
wrongExplanations.D: Silas's installer role makes Lydia's photograph seem stronger. The breaker is that Peter's testimony that he took and recognized his photograph also satisfies the authentication threshold.
